title: Human Resources policy modernization and regulatory attestations
subtitle: Authority for city staff to sign regulatory attestations and a license agreement for an affordable housing initiative.
overview: A special meeting of Council on May 25, 2026 approved a set of modernized Human Resources policies and repealed older policies that had become redundant. The change updates how the City manages its workforce and removes overlapping rules {{vote:m2}}.

Council also authorized named senior staff in engineering, utilities and sustainability to make attestations on the City's involvement in regulatory functions required by federal, provincial and other government-mandated bodies {{vote:m3}}. This lets the City meet reporting requirements that apply to services such as water, wastewater and stormwater.

After a closed session on a security of property matter, Council authorized the General Manager of Development Services to sign a license agreement and related documents, in connection with an affordable housing initiative follow-up {{vote:m4}}. The details were discussed in closed session and are not public in the minutes. The meeting went into closed session to also consider a potential land disposition matter; the minutes report no decision on that matter. The meeting adjourned at 7:11 p.m.

decisions.detail: Council approved the modernized Human Resources policies in Appendix A of report COR-2026-207 and repealed the redundant policies in Appendix B {{vote:m2}}.

Council authorized the Director of Engineering Services, the Manager of Engineering Design and Approval, the Director of Sanitary and Stormwater Utilities, the Manager of Environmental Compliance and Utility Performance, and the Corporate Sustainability Officer to make attestations on the City's regulatory involvement {{vote:m3}}.

Council authorized the General Manager of Development Services to execute a license agreement and related documents, including extensions or amendments, to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor {{vote:m4}}.
